title: At the Doctor's / Ci mbir mi
bridge: In Spanish, to express pain we use 'me duele' + body part (me duele la cabeza). In English, the structure is different: 'I have' + 'a headache' (I have a headache). It's an important change because we don't say 'I hurt my head' for general pain. Also, in English, 'hurt' is used as a verb: 'My head hurts' (my head hurts). Learning to combine 'have' with pain nouns and 'hurt' with subjects will be key to sounding natural.
rule: To talk about symptoms and illnesses in English at A2 level, we mainly use: 1) 'I have' + noun (a headache, a cold, a fever, a cough, a sore throat, a stomachache, etc.) to indicate you have a condition. 2) 'My [body part] hurts' or 'My [body part] is sore' to express pain in a specific part. 3) 'I feel' + adjective (sick, dizzy, tired, etc.) for general states. In questions and short answers, we use 'do/does' (Do you have...? Yes, I do. No, I don't). For recommendations, we use 'should' / 'shouldn't' (You should rest, You shouldn't eat spicy food). Remember that 'hurt' is an irregular verb: hurt - hurt - hurt. Don't use 'me duele' directly; invert the subject: 'My head hurts' (not 'I hurt my head' unless it's an accident). It's also common to use 'I've got' as a contracted form of 'I have got' (I've got a cold). In formal contexts, you can use 'I have a cold'.

concept_examples.text: I have a headache and a sore throat.
concept_examples.translation: Dama naa jëkk ndoxal ak jëkk ndoxal.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ hæv ə ˈhɛdeɪk ənd ə sɔːr θroʊt/

concept_examples.text: My stomach hurts after eating.
concept_examples.translation: Mën naa jëkk ndoxal ci suuf.

concept_examples.text: Do you have a fever?
concept_examples.translation: Dama naa jëkk ndoxal?

concept_examples.text: You should drink a lot of water.
concept_examples.translation: Yaa ngi diwaan ndoxal.
concept_examples.phonetic: /juː ʃʊd drɪŋk ə lɒt əv ˈwɔːtər/

common_error.explanation: The error comes from literally translating 'me duele la cabeza' as 'I hurt my head'. But 'hurt' as a transitive verb means to cause damage (I hurt my head). To express general pain, use 'have a headache' or 'my head hurts'. Remember: 'hurt' as an intransitive verb (without object) describes the sensation of pain, but with a subject the body part (my head hurts). Make sure to use 'have' + noun for common medical conditions.

examples.original: I have a cold.

levels.label: Actions and Advice
levels.translation: Acciones y consejos / Yëpp ak ndigël

examples.original: Take this medicine twice a day.
examples.translation: Jëkk ndoxal laa ko ci ñett ci téere.
examples.note: El verbo 'take' se usa con medicinas, no 'drink' (beber). 'Twice a day' significa dos veces al día.

examples.original: You should rest in bed.
examples.translation: Yaa ngi diwaan ndoxal ci suuf.
examples.note: Ci mbir mi 'should' ak verbe infinitif. Li laa ko wax ci mbir mi dëgg ci 'must' (obligation).

examples.original: I need to make an appointment.
examples.translation: Dama naa jëkk ndoxal.
examples.note: Usa 'make an appointment' para pedir cita médica. 'Need to' + verbo indica necesidad.

levels.label: Describing Pain

examples.original: My back hurts a lot.
examples.translation: Dama naa jëkk ndoxal ci suuf.
examples.note: 'A lot' ci mbir mi. Damaa walla 'my back hurts much' ba noppi 'a'.

examples.original: I have a sharp pain in my chest.

examples.original: My knee is swollen and red.
examples.translation: Mën naa jëkk ndoxal ak jëkk ndoxal.
examples.note: Yëpp 'is' ak adjectif ci mbir mi. Fàtte 'swollen' li laa ko wax ci mbir mi.

title: Booking Accommodation / Reser ak xamxam
bridge: Xaleyi ci suñu yaram ak 'reser' (reservar) mooy jàmm, waaye ci anglèes, 'would like' + 'to book' mooy jubbanti ci mbir ak jàmm. Bëgg naa wax ci 'prepositions': ci suñu yaram, nit ñi ci suñu yaram diñe 'double room' (chambre double). Ci anglèes, mooy 'for' mooy jëfandiku ci 'duration' ('for two nights'), waaye ci suñu yaram mooy 'por dos noches'.
rule: Ndaxte ak reser ak xamxam ci anglèes ci level A2, jëndul ak structures ci: 'I would like to book...' (Dama reser ak...), 'I'd like to make a reservation' (Dama bëgg naa bëgg naa reser). Dafa ñuy jëndul ak 'present simple' ci jëndul ak 'personal information': 'My name is...'. Ci dates, mooy 'on' ak 'days' ('on Monday') ak 'for' ak 'duration' ('for three nights'). Ci jëndul ak 'availability', mooy 'Do you have...?' (Nungi ci...?) waaye 'Is there...?' (Nungi ci...?). Ndi xaleyi ak 'room' ci anglèes: 'single room' (chambre individuelle), 'double room' (chambre double), 'twin room' (chambre à deux lits). Dafa ñuy jëndul ak 'adjectif + sustantif'. Ci jëndul ak 'services', mooy 'with' (ak): 'with a view' (ak yaram), 'with breakfast' (ak petit déjeuner).

concept_examples.translation: Dama bëgg naa reser ak xamxam double room ci 'for two nights'.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd laɪk tə bʊk ə ˈdʌbəl ruːm fɔː tuː naɪts/

concept_examples.phonetic: /haʊ mʌtʃ dʌz ɪt kɒst pɜː naɪt/

common_error.wrong: I want reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct: I would like to reserve a room for two nights.
common_error.correct_alt: I'd like to book a room for two nights.
common_error.explanation: Ci suñu yaram, mooy 'quiero reservar' ak 'querer', waaye ci anglèes 'want' mooy jubbanti ak jàmm. Mooy 'would like' (dama bëgg) mooy jubbanti. Ci anglèes, ci mbir ak 'would like', mooy 'to' + 'verb' ci infinitif: 'I would like to reserve'. Dafa ñuy jëndul 'I want reserve' (without 'to'). Dafa ñuy jëndul 'book' (reser) mooy jubbanti ci hôtels.

examples.original: Can I reserve a room with a balcony?

examples.original: My name is Ana García. I have a reservation.

examples.note: Ci mbir ak 'arrival' ci hôtels, jëndul ak 'name' ak 'reservation'. 'Reservation' mooy jubbanti ak suñu yaram.

examples.original: How much is it per night?
examples.translation: Ngaa ko ci mbir?
examples.note: Jëndul ak 'How much' ci mbir ak 'price'. 'Per night' mooy 'ci mbir'.

examples.original: Does the price include breakfast?
examples.translation: Price mooy include breakfast?

rule: Pou jëfandikoo ci banku ukk yaatuwaay, duggal naa jëkkër gi ci mbir ci 'maangi yàgg' (maangi leen) ci 'maangi ko' ci 'maangi ci'... Ci mbir ci 'maangi yàgg' (maangi leen) ci 'maangi ko' ci 'maangi ci'... Ci mbir ci 'maangi yàgg' (maangi leen) ci 'maangi ko' ci 'maangi ci'... Ci mbir ci 'maangi yàgg' (maangi leen) ci 'maangi ko'.

title: At the post office / Ngone bu poste ak servic
bridge: Ci angale, pour exprimer des besoins et des demandes dans un bureau de poste, on utilise des structures modales comme 'I need to' ou 'I'd like to', tandis qu'en espagnol on utilise 'necesito' ou 'quiero'. De plus, en anglais le verbe 'send' s'utilise avec la préposition 'to' pour indiquer la destination (send something to someone), tandis qu'en espagnol on dit 'enviar algo a alguien'. Faites attention à l'ordre des mots dans des questions comme 'How much does it cost?', où en espagnol on demande '¿Cuánto cuesta?'.
rule: Pour parler des envois et des services postaux en anglais à niveau A2, utilisez ces modèles: 1) 'I need to + verbe' (necesito + infinitif) pour exprimer un besoin, par exemple 'I need to send this package.' 2) 'I'd like to + verbe' (me gustaría + infinitif) pour des demandes polies, par exemple 'I'd like to buy some stamps.' 3) 'How much is/are...?' et 'How much does it cost?' pour demander des prix, par exemple 'How much is the shipping?' 4) Utilisation de 'to' après des verbes comme 'send' et 'mail' pour indiquer le destinataire, par exemple 'Send it to my friend.' 5) Questions avec 'where' et 'when' pour des informations sur les services, par exemple 'Where can I pick up my package?' N'oubliez pas qu'en anglais l'adjectif précède le nom (registered mail), contrairement à l'espagnol qui peut le suivre (correo certificado).

title: Renting a Flat / Alugilu ndaw
bridge: Ci waxoon wi, ngoneel seen alugil, amoon na ne 'alugil' ba 'rent', te seen taxawu ndaw seen alugil, amoon na ne 'dey na' ba 'dey alugil'. Ci angale, amoon na ne 'rent' ngir verb ba nom, 'rent' (alugil), 'available' ba 'for rent' ngir taxawu ndaw seen alugil. Waxtaane ci ngoneel: ci angale, amoon na ne 'rent an apartment' (sente preposicion), waaye ci waxoon wi, amoon na ne 'alugil ndaw'. Ci angale, anonte seen alugil, amoon na ne struktiir pasif 'is for rent' ba 'is available', waaye ci waxoon wi, amoon na ne 'dey alugil' ba 'dey na'.
rule: Ngoneel seen alugil ci angale, A2, waxtaane: (1) Verb 'to rent' (alugil) ak forme yi: rent / rents / renting / rented. (2) Preposicion 'for' ak nom 'rent' ngir taxawu ndaw seen alugil: 'for rent' (alugil). (3) Adjetif 'available' (dey na) ngir wax ci ndaw dey na. (4) Vocabulaire: 'apartment' (ndaw), 'flat' (ndaw, ci angale britanike), 'landlord' (jambaar), 'tenant' (alugilu), 'deposit' (garanti), 'rent' (alugil), 'lease' (kontraat). (5) Ngoneel seen wax, amoon na ne 'How much is the rent?' (Naka alugil?) ba 'Is it furnished?' (Dee amul?). Ci struktiir, waxtaane ci angale, adjetif yi seen taxaw ci nom: 'a small apartment', defte 'an apartment small'.

title: Making small talk at a party / Waxtaanu taxaw ci paj
bridge: Àddina wolof, dégg naa waxtaanu paj, ñu ngi déy defar 'Naka ngi def?' ob 'Maa ngi fi rekk?', ak ñu ngi ngi ci tàkk defar 'Waxtaanu' ngir wàcc-wàcc. Àddina angle, ñu ngi def 'How are you?' ak 'How's it going?' ob 'What's up?' ngir waxtaanu ci paj. Dégg naa waxtaanu paj, ñu ngi def 'I'm good, thanks' ngir waxtaanu, waaye ñu ngi def it 'Naka ngi def?' ngir waxtaanu ci paj
rule: Waxtaanu paj, ngi def 'Hey, how's it going?' ob 'What's up?' (defar: 'Not much, you?'). Ngir defar, ngi def 'I'm [name], nice to meet you'. Ngir defar lu ñu ngi wax, ngi def 'Would you like something to drink?' (ngir defar lu ñu ngi wax) ob 'Do you want a drink?' (ngir defar lu ñu ngi wax). Ngir waxtaanu, ngi def 'I like...' / 'I don't like...'. Ngir defar, ngi def 'I agree with you'. Defar 'How are you?' ngir waxtaanu, ngi def 'I'm good', 'I'm fine', 'Pretty good'. Ngir defar, ngi def 'It was nice talking to you' ob 'See you later'

title: Describing your hometown / Defar ndakaru bu bees
bridge: Ci inglée, defar ndakaru bu bees, ngi ciy verbe 'to be' defar ndax how (big, small, quiet) and 'there is/there are' defar ndax lu bopp, ngir lu tol. Ci spañol, ngi defar 'es grande' or 'hay un parque', pero ci inglée, defar 'there is' defar lu singular and 'there are' defar lu plural. Ngir lu boppe, defar lu ndakaru bu bees, ngi defar 'My city is big'. Lu ñaan hispanohablantes defar naan lu ñaari 'there is/are' or defar lu adjetivo defar lu sustantivo, defar 'the city big' defar lu 'the big city'.
rule:
Defar ndakaru bu bees ci inglée A2, ngi ciy patrones yii:

1. **Sujeto + verbo 'to be' (am/is/are) + adjetivo**: Defar ndax characteristics generales. Ejemplo: 'My town is small.' (Ndakaru bu bees jàpp na). 
   - Ci pronombres: I am, you are, he/she/it is, we are, they are. 
   - Adjetivos defar lu sustantivo defar lu modifise: 'a big city', defar lu 'a city big'. 

2. **There is / There are**: Defar ndax lu bopp ci ndakaru bu bees. 
   - There is + sustantivo singular/contable defar lu: 'There is a park.' (Hay un parque). 
   - There are + sustantivo plural: 'There are two schools.' (Hay dos escuelas). 
   - Defar lu negativo: There isn't / There aren't: 'There isn't a cinema.' (No hay cine). 
   - Defar lu preguntas: Is there...? Are there...? (¿Hay...?). 

3. **Preposiciones de lugar**: Defar ndax lu bopp ci ndakaru bu bees. 
   - 'in the center' (ci ndaw), 'on the corner' (ci kër), 'near' (ci diggu), 'next to' (ci diggu). 

4. **Verbos de acción**: 'You can see', 'you can find', 'there is' defar lu defar ndax 'se puede encontrar'. 

5. **Conectores**: Ngir lu boppe, defar 'and' defar lu unir ideas and 'but' defar lu contrastar: 'My town is small but beautiful.' (Ndakaru bu bees jàpp na, waaye defar lu). 

Defar A2, ngi defar lu frases simples and directas. Defar lu plural 'there is' defar lu 'there are' – defar lu 'there is many shops'.

Ci inglée, defar lu existencia, defar lu natural defar lu 'there is' defar lu 'to have'.

title: Talking About Hobbies / Waxtaan ci waxi ajandé
bridge: Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «gustar» walla «encantar» ak mbooloomi yeneen (mëgë «me gusta», «te gusta»), ak ñu ngi def ko «me gusta + infinitivo». Ànglès, verbe «like» dafay wax ci mëgë : «I like + -ing» walla «I like + to + verbe». Bokk nañu xam-xam, ànglès, verbe «like» dafay wax ci mëgë, waaye «do» dafay wax ci mëgë lu tolloo ci waxi ajandé (What do you do in your free time?). Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «¿Qué haces en tu tiempo libre?».
rule: Waxtaan ci waxi ajandé ànglès (niveau A2) : jublu «like», «love», «enjoy» walla «prefer» ak mbooloomi yeneen (mëgë «I like music», «I love playing soccer»). Ñu ngi def ko «be interested in» + mbooloomi yeneen (mëgë «I'm interested in photography»). Waxtaan, jublu «What do you like doing?» walla «What do you do in your free time?». Freqensi, jublu adverbe «always», «usually», «sometimes», «never» ci mëgë verbe (mëgë «I usually read»). Ñu ngi def ko prepozisyon «in» (in my free time), «on» (on weekends, on Mondays) ak «at» (at home, at the weekend – ànglès britannique). Mëgë : «do» dafay wax ci mëgë lu tolloo ci waxi ajandé (mëgë «I like», dafay wax «I do like» ànd ak mëgë def ko)

concept_examples.translation: Mëgë waxtaan ci musiqa.

concept_examples.translation: Yëngu-yëngu gu yëkkatu ci tenis.

common_error.explanation: Mëgë def ko lu tolloo ci waxi ajandé, àdaxna wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «me gusta» ak infinitivo, ak yërëm yépp, ñu ngi def ko ànglès, lu tolloo ci waxi ajandé, «like», «love», «enjoy» ak verbe -ing (mëgë «I like playing»), walla infinitivo ak «to» (mëgë «I like to play»), waaye dafay wax infinitivo lu tolloo ci «to». Mëgë def ko, ñu ngi def ko : after «like», jublu verbe -ing : «I like playing». Mëgë def ko, ñu ngi def ko «I like to play», waaye dafay wax lu tolloo ci mëgë.

examples.original: I love reading books.
examples.translation: Mëgë waxtaan ci bu xëcc
examples.note: Jublu «love» + -ing, mëgë waxtaan ci lii waxtaan. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «encantar».

examples.translation: Yëngu-yëngu gu yëkkatu ci piktir
examples.note: 'Enjoy' dafay wax ci mëgë verbe -ing. Dafay wax «enjoy to paint».

examples.translation: Mëgë dafay waxtaan ci xëcc
examples.note: Mëgë def ko, jublu «don't» + «like» + -ing. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «no me gusta».

levels.label: Asking Others About Hobbies

examples.note: Ànglès, jublu «go to» + liir. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «ir al cine» ak «a».

examples.original: I often watch TV in the evening.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈɒfən wɒtʃ ˌtiːˈviː ɪn ðə ˈiːvnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Mëgë waxtaan ci télé ci gu bëj-gànnaar
examples.note: Adverbe freqensi (often, usually, always) dafay wax ci mëgë verbe. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «a menudo».

examples.original: I prefer playing video games to reading.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ prɪˈfɜː ˈpleɪɪŋ ˈvɪdiəʊ ɡeɪmz tə ˈriːdɪŋ/
examples.translation: Mëgë waxtaan ci xëcc ci vidéo-jéw ak bu xëcc
examples.note: Mëgë def ko, jublu «prefer A to B», ak lii waxi ajandé -ing. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «prefiero X a Y».

examples.original: On Sundays, I usually go for a walk.
examples.phonetic: /ɒn ˈsʌndeɪz aɪ ˈjuːʒuəli ɡəʊ fər ə wɔːk/
examples.translation: Dipar, mëgë waxtaan ci wàll garab
examples.note: Jublu «on» ci aw yépp. Àdaxna, wàllula waxtaan ci waxi ajandé, ñi ngi ci jublu «los domingos».
